chapter: Japan trip, publishing and early influences
title: Record companies want half the publishing
summary: Gil says companies demand half the publishing rights, and Johnston compares it to earlier cases of Black composers being cheated.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I was so tickled when you said you came back with .......

Even with the composers. A lot of times a record company wont release your music unless you give them half the publishing. That happens now. I took my tapes the other day, I have two tapes, a USA and a Japanese tape that I wanted to play for you (on Sunday?). And this man said he liked them very much but he said he had to have half the publishing. And I didn't write all the numbers, so he would have to contact all the different players and see if they want to do it, you know, which I don't think they would.
Oh some of them [insult] you with, well this is private, you have to use it as a stepping stone (for your career... ?). You hope that some day you won't have to give them the next batch ( ?).

Well of course thinking that this is happening even now and to people like you makes me think about what used to happen to those negro composers years ago when, I know some of them have told me really horrendous stories. Somebody would get them together to make a demonstration tape or disc in those days and later on they'd be walking
the street you know, and hear the record. It's been produced commercially and they don't have a penny from it. Not a penny.
Well that went on for years. It went on for years. The style, it wasn't an exact copy, it was a copy of the style. ( ? )
